rules.rule: Proof of service must state the papers served, the person served, the date, time and place, and that service was made by an authorized person in an authorized manner
quote: Proof of service shall specify the papers served, the person who was served and the date, time,
set forth facts showing that the service was made by an authorized person and in an authorized manner.
rules.note: 306(a) itself contains no affidavit wording; it governs the content of proof of service. The affidavit requirement comes from the order (p.6), which cites 306(a).

rules.rule: Form of proof: a certificate when a sheriff or other authorized public officer serves; otherwise an affidavit of the person who made service (signed and sworn by that person)
quote: Proof of service shall be in the form of a certificate if the service is made by a sheriff
or other authorized public officer
rules.note: Retrieved 2026-10-25 via WebFetch excerpt. The affidavit clause for any other person was paraphrased by the tool, not quoted (summary).

rules.rule: Service within 120 days after commencement; court may extend on good cause or in the interest of justice
quote: shall be made within one hundred twenty days after the commencement of the action or proceeding
upon good cause shown or in the interest of justice, extend the time for service
rules.note: Most recent revision shown is 2026-04-24; the content of that amendment was not reviewed. The order extended time to 120 days from entry. 306-b does not define when service is complete.

rules.rule: Court-directed service when 308(1), (2) and (4) are impracticable
quote: in such manner as the court, upon motion without notice, directs,
if service is impracticable under paragraphs one, two and four of this section.
rules.note: Per WebFetch, paragraph 5 contains no language on when service is complete and does not mention filing proof of service; completion therefore comes from the court's order (L1: 'deemed complete upon such filing' of the affidavit).

rules.rule: Contrast: deliver-and-mail service is complete ten days after proof is filed
quote: service shall be complete ten days after such filing
rules.note: Not applicable to L1; shown to explain why completion under 308(5) depends on the order.

rules.rule: Appearance within 20 days of service, or 30 days after service is complete when served under 308(2)-(5) and other listed provisions (used here because the order did not set a different period)
quote: subdivision two, three, four or five of section 308
the appearance shall be made within thirty days after service is complete

rules.rule: When summons and complaint are served together under 308(2)-(5) (and other listed provisions), the answer is due within thirty days after service is complete (used here because the order did not set a different period)
quote: or if service of the summons and complaint is made pursuant to section 303, paragraphs two,
three, four or five of section 308, or sections 313, 314 or 315, service of an answer shall be made
within thirty days after service is complete.
rules.note: Retrieved 2026-10-25 via WebFetch excerpt. Parallels 320(a) for the answer when the complaint is served with the summons.

rules.rule: Partial list: a default application must include proof of service of the summons and complaint, and proof of the facts, the default and the amount due by affidavit. Other default requirements (e.g., an SCRA affidavit) are not covered here
quote: Proof. On any application for judgment by default, the applicant shall file proof of service of the summons
proof of the facts constituting the claim, the default and the amount due, including, if applicable,
by affidavit made by the party
rules.note: Per WebFetch the phrase 'affidavit of service' does not appear in (f); it requires 'proof of service of the summons and the complaint'.

rules.rule: If the plaintiff does not take proceedings for a default judgment within one year after the default, the court dismisses the complaint as abandoned, unless sufficient cause is shown
quote: Default not entered within one year. If the plaintiff fails to take proceedings for the entry of judgment
within one year after the default
the court shall not enter judgment but shall dismiss the complaint as abandoned, without costs,
unless sufficient cause is shown why
rules.note: Exception excerpt retrieved 2026-10-25 via WebFetch from the same page; the words after "why" were not retrieved.

ruleStatusDefinitions.excerpt-verified: Every string in "quote" was returned verbatim from the official nysenate.gov page for that section. Only the excerpt is checked, not the full section.
ruleStatusDefinitions.summary: The "rule" text is a paraphrase. Any part not covered by a quote is not checked against the statute.

precedents.point: Service by airdropping NFTs hyperlinked to a website with the papers to three wallet addresses (CPLR 308(5)); service complete on filing of the affidavit. A trial-court order on an unopposed motion.
precedents.note: Signed 2025-06-09, entered 2025-06-11 (NYSCEF 21). A web search lists it as 2025 NY Slip Op 25143 (one search summary also gave 87 Misc 3d 950). The official text was not retrieved: on 2026-10-25 nycourts.gov returned 403, law.justia.com returned 403, Casetext returned 410, CourtListener search returned no results and Google Scholar returned a captcha. The order itself was read from the ag.ny.gov PDF.
